commands.review_summary:
The PR defers initial ACP session snapshot and available-command notifications until after `newSession` and `resumeSession` return, with lifecycle and NDJSON ordering tests.

PR surface: Source +12, Tests +585. Total +597 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible: await `newSession` or `resumeSession`, immediately call `closeSession` for that id, then allow the scheduled timer to run. The callback has no cancellation or current-session guard.

target.title: fix(acp): defer session snapshot update after newSession/resumeSession result
target.body:
## Summary

ACP lifecycle timing: session/new and session/resume JSON-RPC responses must be written to wire before session/update notifications. setTimeout(0) defers notifications past the synchronous handler return and response serialization.

- Problem: Initial session_info_update and available_commands_update notifications could arrive in the same microtask as the JSON-RPC response, making wire ordering non-deterministic
- Solution: setTimeout(0) delays notifications to the next event-loop tick, guaranteeing response-first wire ordering
- What changed:
  - `src/acp/translator.ts`: newSession and resumeSession notification scheduling changed to setTimeout(0)
  - `src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts`: 3x no-promise-executor-return lint fix + ordering assertions
  - `src/acp/translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts` (new): real ndJsonStream byte-level ordering proof
- What did NOT change: Gateway protocol layer, session storage, prompt handling, other ACP handlers

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related: Codex review comments on PR #109973
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

ACP clients start interacting immediately after receiving a session/new or session/resume JSON-RPC response. If a session_info_update notification arrives on the wire before the response, clients may observe incomplete session state. The response must always be written to the NDJSON stream before any notification.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: newSession/resumeSession JSON-RPC response arrives before session/update notification at the NDJSON transport layer
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.15.0, branch `fix/acp-bridge-session-order`, OpenClaw `2026.7.2`
- Exact commands run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts src/acp/translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts
```

### NDJSON Wire-Level Transcript — newSession

The proof test connects `AcpGatewayAgent` over a real `ndJsonStream` + `AgentSideConnection` and captures every NDJSON byte the agent writes. 4 lines in arrival order:

```
[0] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":1,"agentCapabilities":{"loadSession":true,"promptCapabilities":{"image":true,"audio":false,"embeddedContext":true},"mcpCapabilities":{"http":false,"sse":false},"sessionCapabilities":{"list":{},"resume":{},"close":{}}},"agentInfo":{"name":"openclaw-acp","title":"OpenClaw ACP Gateway","version":"2026.7.2"},"authMethods":[]}}
    ↑ initialize RESPONSE

[1] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"sessionId":"c90b4221-b561-46d3-bee0-e316a82bfd47","configOptions":[...], "modes":{...}}}
    ↑ session/new RESULT ← arrives FIRST

[2] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"c90b4221-...","update":{"sessionUpdate":"session_info_update","title":"acp-bridge:...","updatedAt":null,"_meta":{"sessionKey":"acp-bridge:...","kind":"unknown"}}}}
    ↑ session_info_update NOTIFICATION ← arrives AFTER response

[3] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"c90b4221-...","update":{"sessionUpdate":"available_commands_update","availableCommands":[]}}}
    ↑ available_commands_update NOTIFICATION
```

**Ordering proof**: [1] response index < [2] notification index. responseIndex < updateIndex ✓

### NDJSON Wire-Level Transcript — resumeSession

```
[0] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":1,"agentCapabilities":{...},"agentInfo":{"name":"openclaw-acp","title":"OpenClaw ACP Gateway","version":"2026.7.2"},"authMethods":[]}}
    ↑ initialize RESPONSE

[1] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"configOptions":[...], "modes":{"currentModeId":"adaptive","availableModes":[...]}}}
    ↑ session/resume RESULT ← arrives FIRST

[2] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"agent:main:order-proof","update":{"sessionUpdate":"session_info_update","title":"Order proof","updatedAt":"2026-07-19T02:35:54.422Z","_meta":{"sessionKey":"agent:main:order-proof","kind":"direct","spawnedWorkspaceDir":"/tmp"}}}}
    ↑ session_info_update NOTIFICATION ← arrives AFTER response

[3] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"agent:main:order-proof","update":{"sessionUpdate":"available_commands_update","availableCommands":[]}}}
    ↑ available_commands_update NOTIFICATION
```

**Ordering proof**: [1] response index < [2] notification index. responseIndex < updateIndex ✓

### Test Results

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts src/acp/translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts

 ✓ |acp| src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts (15 tests) 256ms
 ✓ |acp| src/acp/translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts (2 tests) 11609ms
     ✓ newSession: JSON-RPC response line precedes session/update notification in NDJSON stream
     ✓ resumeSession: JSON-RPC response line precedes session/update notification in NDJSON stream

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. NDJSON transcript confirms: session/new and session/resume JSON-RPC result lines always precede session/update notification lines
  2. 2 new ordering-proof tests pass
  3. All 15 existing lifecycle tests pass (no regression)
  4. 3x `no-promise-executor-return` lint violations fixed
- What was not tested: Real Gateway WebSocket connection flow (requires Gateway infra); proof covers ACP stdio/in-memory transport only

## Root Cause (if applicable)

ACP lifecycle notifications (session_info_update, available_commands_update) were sent at the synchronous tail of newSession()/resumeSession(), in the same microtask as the JSON-RPC response. The SDK's ndJsonStream serializes messages in call order, making response-vs-notification wire ordering non-deterministic without an explicit boundary.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- All 15 existing lifecycle tests pass
- 2 new NDJSON byte-level ordering tests validate wire order
- Ordering stability can be verified by repeated test runs

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. Internal message ordering fix only — behavior remains identical from the client perspective (client always receives response before notification, same as before, now guaranteed).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: newSession NDJSON ordering (single input variant), resumeSession NDJSON ordering (single input variant), lint compliance
- Edge cases checked: Notification never arriving (session_info_update missing) — test framework still validates response validity
- What you did NOT verify: E2E ACP session over real Gateway WebSocket

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — API response format unchanged, notification content unchanged, only ordering is now guaranteed
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — `setTimeout(0)` is the minimal-invasions approach. It creates a deterministic event-loop boundary between synchronous response writing and asynchronous notification dispatch without refactoring the entire notification scheduling architecture.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: queueMicrotask() — still executes before response serialization; Promise microtask scheduling — non-deterministic ordering within same microtask; setImmediate — semantically equivalent but Node-specific

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: o3 / claude-4.5-sonnet
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: NDJSON proof test and lint fix AI-assisted

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: setTimeout(0) introduces async delay (~0-4ms) before notifications become visible
- **Mitigation**: Non-critical path: notifications are auxiliary info (session title, available commands). Clients do not depend on them to proceed. The response itself carries all required fields (sessionId, configOptions, modes).
- **Compatibility impact**: None — notifications still fire, just a few event-loop ticks later
